content: If you are close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage Instructions: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Voriconazole is used to treat a variety of fungal infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as azole antifungals. How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting voriconazole and each time you get a refill. The dosage and length of treatment depend on your medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and other medications you may be taking. For optimal results, take this antifungal at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Nausea, vomiting, and headache may occur. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, voriconazole may cause serious (possibly fatal) liver disease. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are also rare. Voriconazole commonly causes mild rashes, which are usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild rash and a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking voriconazole, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., lactose) that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Voriconazole may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (e.g., diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This drug may cause vision changes. Voriconazole may make you more sensitive to the sun and increase your risk of skin cancer, especially with long-term use. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using voriconazole, as it may harm an unborn baby. Ask about reliable forms of birth control while using this medication. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Voriconazole can slow the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of voriconazole from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include butalbital, efavirenz, mitotane, rifamycins (e.g., rifabutin, rifampin), ritonavir, secobarbital, and certain drugs used to treat seizures (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital). Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Additional Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., liver/kidney function, blood mineral levels) should be performed before starting this medication and periodically while taking it. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete and personalized guidance.
